paragraphs.source_en: The master continued: “What people today call self-awareness is, one might say, an excessive awareness that a sharply cut gulf of interest lies between oneself and others. As civilization advances, this self-awareness grows keener day by day, until in the end even the raising of a hand or the taking of a step can no longer be done naturally. A man named Henley, criticizing Stevenson, said that whenever Stevenson entered a room with a mirror, he had to look at his reflection each time he passed before it; he was a man unable to forget himself for even a moment. That criticism in fact describes the tendency of the present age very well. Asleep I think of myself, awake I think of myself; this self clings everywhere, so human conduct becomes only artificial and cramped, binds itself tight, and makes the world feel painful. It is just like the state of young men and women at a marriage interview, restless from morning to night. Words such as leisurely and composed have become only written characters on paper, words without real substance or meaning. In this respect, people of the present age have become spy-like and thief-like. A spy’s work is to avoid being noticed and furtively seek advantage for himself, so he naturally must possess a strong self-awareness. A thief too is always anxious about whether he will be discovered or caught, and so he too is compelled to have a strong self-awareness. People today, asleep or awake, are always calculating what benefits them and what harms them; their self-awareness is as strong as that of spies and thieves. For twenty-four hours they are restless and furtive, and until the moment they go to the grave they cannot gain a moment’s peace; such is the mentality of modern man. It is a curse of civilization, and utterly ridiculous.”

paragraphs.source_en: Dokusen said, “Indeed, that is an interesting explanation.” When a question like this came up, he was never a man to hold back his opinion. He said, “Kushami’s explanation suits my own view very well. People in the past taught others to forget themselves; people today teach them not to forget themselves, and that is completely different. For twenty-four hours the consciousness called self fills everything. For that reason, not a single moment in twenty-four hours is peaceful. It is always a scorching hell. If one asks what medicine under heaven is best, there is no medicine better than forgetting oneself. ‘Entering no-self under the moon at the third watch’ sings precisely of this highest state. People today lack natural feeling even when they show kindness to others. The conduct the English boast of as nice is in fact often self-awareness stretched to the breaking point. They say that when the British sovereign went to India and shared a table with an Indian prince, the prince, not realizing he was before the sovereign, followed his own country’s custom and took potatoes onto his plate with his hand, then afterward blushed crimson with shame. The sovereign, as if nothing had happened, also took potatoes onto his own plate with two fingers...”
